messages.subject: Log transformation of positive data
parts:
Dear all,
 
I want to model some data that is always positive, so I take log-transformation and model it with spde model saying
log(y) = intercept + x, x is the spde GF ..
What I do is,
stk_est <- inla.stack(data=list(resp=log(trainset[,3])), A=list(A_est,1),
                            effects=list(i=1:spde1$n.spde,intercept=rep(1,nrow(A_est))), tag='est')
stk_prd <- inla.stack(data=list(resp=NA), A=list(A_prd,1),
                            effects=list(i=1:spde1$n.spde,intercept=rep(1,nrow(A_prd))), tag='prd')
stk_full <- inla.stack(stk_est,stk_prd)
res <- inla(resp ~ 0 + intercept + f(i, model=spde1),...)
 
Then I can get posterior mean of the response by exp(res$summary.fitted.values$mean[ind_prd]), can I? And how can I get the correct posterior standard deviation of the response?  Do you have some link function which can be considered in the inla inference so that we do not need to do the post-processing?
 
Thanks a lot!
 
Best wishes,
Ming

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Log transformation of positive data
parts:
On 19 June 2014 11:58, ming li <ming.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
> log(y) = intercept + x, x is the spde GF ..

<cut correct looking code>

I'll assume that you have the line
ind_prd <- inla.stack.index(stk_full, tag="prd")$data
as well.

> Then I can get posterior mean of the response by
> exp(res$summary.fitted.values$mean[ind_prd]), can I?

Not quite, but close. Note that exp(E(x|y)) is not equal to E(exp(x)|y), so
be careful with transforming expectations. It's much safer to use the posterior
quantiles instead, as they do transform cleanly, so for a pure point
estimate you can do

exp(res$summary.fitted.values[ind_prd,"0.5quant"])

to get the posterior median of the response.

> And how can I get the
> correct posterior standard deviation of the response?

You can use inla.emarginal() and related functions for computing
transformed properties of the posterior, operating on
"res$marginals.fitted.values".

Finn
